jobs.occupation: Software Engineer (C++)
jobs.description:
Want to build C++ software that helps power the next generation of autonomous and unmanned systems?At Robotto, we build advanced autonomy and software solutions for drones and unmanned systems. Our technology brings together computer vision, C++ software, autonomy, embedded systems and real-world product development.

We are looking for a C++ Software Engineer to join our engineering team and contribute to the software that connects and powers different parts of Robotto’s technology platform.This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys building reliable systems, solving complex technical problems and seeing their software move beyond development into real-world operation.

The role
You will develop and maintain C++ software across Robotto’s software ecosystem, working on applications and services that support the operation, communication and coordination of our unmanned systems.Depending on the project, your work may span different parts of our platform—from software running alongside our autonomous systems to applications used to configure, control and interact with them.You will work closely with engineers across computer vision, autonomy, embedded software, electronics and testing to develop new capabilities, integrate components and continuously improve the reliability and performance of our systems.

What you will do

• 
Design, develop and maintain high-quality software primarily in C++.

• 
Build software used across our drone and unmanned-systems platform.

• 
Develop reliable communication and data flows between different software and hardware components.

• 
Work on performance-sensitive and potentially real-time or near-real-time applications.

• 
Integrate software with APIs, networking components, sensors and wider system infrastructure.

• 
Debug complex issues across interconnected software systems and identify root causes.

• 
Contribute to software architecture and technical design decisions.

• 
Write maintainable, testable and well-structured production code.

• 
Participate in code reviews, testing, documentation and continuous improvement of our engineering practices.

• 
Collaborate closely with computer vision, embedded, autonomy and hardware engineers.

• 
Support integration and testing on real systems and drone platforms..

What success could look like in your first 3–6 months

• 
You have developed a strong understanding of Robotto’s software architecture and how the different parts of our platform work together.

• 
You are contributing production-quality C++ code to our products.

• 
You have taken ownership of features or components from development through integration and testing.

• 
You are successfully debugging and solving issues across interconnected systems.

• 
You are contributing to improved reliability, maintainability and performance of our software.

• 
You have become a trusted technical partner within the engineering team.

What we are looking forWe are looking for a strong software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems and building software that interacts with real systems.

• 
Strong professional experience developing production-quality software in C++, with a solid understanding of modern software engineering practices.

• 
Solid understanding of software architecture, data structures, algorithms and object-oriented design.

• 
Experience developing multi-component or distributed software systems.

• 
Experience with networking, inter-process communication, APIs or communication protocols is highly relevant.

• 
Good understanding of concurrency, multithreading and performance considerations in C++.

• 
Experience with debugging, testing, version control and modern software development practices.

• 
Experience with Linux-based development environments is an advantage.

• 
Experience with robotics, drones, autonomous systems, defence technology or other complex technical products is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• 
Experience working with software that interfaces with hardware or real-world systems is an advantage.

• 
Professional fluency in English.

• 
A degree in computer science, software engineering, robotics or a related field is preferred; equivalent practical experience is equally welcome.

Please apply even if you don't meet every single point. We are interested in what you can bring to the team, your ability to learn and your motivation to work on the challenges we are solving.

Who you are
Beyond your technical or professional experience, we care about how you work and collaborate.You:

• 
Are curious and enjoy solving complex problems.

• 
Take ownership and follow things through.

• 
Communicate openly about progress, challenges and risks.

• 
Are comfortable in a growing company where priorities can evolve.

• 
Enjoy collaborating with people across different disciplines.

• 
Value testing, learning and continuous improvement.

• 
Want to contribute rather than simply execute a predefined set of tasks.

Why join Robotto?
Robotto is building advanced autonomy technology for drones and unmanned systems, working at the intersection of software, hardware, computer vision, autonomy and real-world operations.You will be joining Robotto at an exciting stage of our journey as we continue to grow our team, technology and products.

Our teams work across software, computer vision, control, electronics, hardware and real-world testing. This means you will work closely with people from different technical disciplines and see how your work contributes to the wider product.

We are an ambitious and collaborative team, and we value people who take ownership, challenge ideas constructively and want to help build both great technology and a great company.This is not a role where everything is already defined. You will have the opportunity to:

• 
Work on challenging technology with real-world applications.

• 
Have meaningful ownership and influence over your area.

• 
Work closely with talented colleagues across multiple disciplines.

• 
See your work move from an idea or prototype into real-world use.

• 
Help shape how we work as the company continues to grow.

Our hiring process
We want our hiring process to be straightforward, transparent and conversational.

1. Introductory conversation with People & Culture
A chance for us to learn more about you and for you to learn more about Robotto, the role and what we are looking for.

2. Meeting with the Hiring Manager
A deeper conversation about your experience, skills and approach to the role

.3. Technical / Role-specific discussion
Depending on the position, this may include a technical discussion, practical exercise, case or live scenario relevant to the work you would be doing at Robotto.

4. Leadership meeting
A conversation with a member of our leadership team to explore mutual fit and give you another opportunity to learn about Robotto and where we are going

.5. Offer
If there is a strong mutual fit, we will move forward with an offer.The exact process may vary slightly depending on the role.

Interested?
If this sounds like an opportunity you would like to explore, we would love to hear from you.Apply through our careers page and tell us a little about yourself, your experience and why Robotto interests you.

Equal opportunity
At Robotto, we want to build a team where different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives are valued.We welcome applications from qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, nationality, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or other characteristics protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
OFFICE MANAGER WANTED FOR OUR OFFICE IN ØSTERBRO

Are you service-minded, organised, and the kind of person who keeps the office running smoothly – even when things get busy?

We are looking for a dedicated Office Manager for a permanent position at our office in Østerbro, Copenhagen.

As our Office Manager, you will be a central part of our day-to-day operations and play an important role in ensuring that the office runs professionally and efficiently.

We operate a staffing agency where the pace can be fast. Phones are ringing, candidates are coming and going, and there are always people, appointments, and tasks that need to be coordinated.

That is why we are looking for someone who thrives on responsibility, enjoys working with people, and appreciates a varied working day.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

You will be responsible for the day-to-day running of the office. Your responsibilities will include:

• Daily office administration and coordination
• Welcoming candidates, temporary workers, clients, and other visitors
• Answering phone calls and emails
• Managing calendars and coordinating meetings and interviews
• Preparing meeting rooms and office facilities
• Ordering office supplies, refreshments, and other necessities
• Handling post, parcels, and deliveries
• Liaising with suppliers and business partners
• Providing practical support with the onboarding of new employees and temporary workers
• Updating and maintaining administrative information and documents
• Planning internal events and social activities
• Handling administrative and practical ad hoc tasks

You will also be an important source of support for our consultants and management team, helping to create structure and ensure smooth day-to-day operations.

WHO ARE YOU?

Above all, we are looking for someone who takes ownership of the office and wants to make a positive difference in the workplace.

You notice what needs to be done, take initiative, and make sure tasks are followed through from start to finish.

We imagine that you:

• Are organised and have a strong sense of overview
• Are outgoing, positive, and service-minded
• Take responsibility and are comfortable working independently
• Enjoy working with people and communicate professionally
• Are able to manage several tasks at the same time
• Thrive in an environment where the day does not always go according to plan
• Have good IT skills
• Communicate confidently in Danish and preferably also in English
• Contribute positively to the atmosphere and sense of community in the office

Previous experience as an Office Manager, receptionist, administrative coordinator, PA, or office assistant is an advantage. However, your personality, way of working, and willingness to take responsibility are just as important to us.

WHAT DO WE OFFER?

You will have a permanent base at our office in Østerbro and become an important part of our internal team.

At the same time, we believe in flexibility and freedom with responsibility. Depending on your tasks and by prior agreement, there will therefore be an opportunity to work from home a few days per week. Tasks that require your physical presence will, of course, be carried out from our office in Østerbro.

With us, you can expect a working day filled with people, responsibility, and plenty of variety. There is a short path from idea to action, and you will have the opportunity to shape both your role and the way we run our office.

We offer:

• A permanent position based at our office in Østerbro
• The opportunity to work from home a few days per week
• Flexibility and freedom with responsibility
• A central role with responsibility and influence
• A varied working day
• Close collaboration with both colleagues and management
• An informal, fast-paced working environment
• Opportunities for professional and personal development

Location: Østerbro, Copenhagen / opportunity to work from home
Position: Full-time
Start date: As soon as possible / by agreement
Salary: Based on qualifications

COULD YOU BE THE PERSON WHO KEEPS OUR OFFICE RUNNING SMOOTHLY?

Send your CV and a short application to info@manora.dk.

Please tell us a little about yourself and why you could see yourself becoming part of our team.

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire once we have found the right candidate.

We look forward to hearing from you!

PLEASE NOTE: APPLICATIONS AND ENQUIRIES WILL ONLY BE ACCEPTED IN WRITING.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in High Frequency Switch-Mode Power Supplies
jobs.description:
The Digital and High-Frequency Electronics (DHFE) section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, based at the university campus in Odense, seeks outstanding individuals for full-time Assistant Professor positions in Power Electronics, focusing on power management for electronic and computing devices and systems. Successful applicants are expected to contribute to the development of academic programs and the research community. Applicants should have a PhD in Power Electronics or a closely related field. 

The DHFE section focuses on conducting research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communication, utilizing cutting-edge reconfigurable computing and sensors. The aim is to develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions that solve technology-related challenges in fields such as autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grid, and healthcare.

Applicants are expected to establish and maintain a research program in high-frequency power electronics and power management for computation, along with low-voltage electronic systems. The position emphasizes converter and power-management for computing platforms and resource-constrained applications, including battery-operated, energy-harvesting, mobile, autonomous, embedded, and sensor-based systems.

The section is a vital component of our Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Science, and Master of Science programs in Electrical and Electronics Engineering in Odense. Currently, the section focuses on three research fields: 1) Drones for Infrastructure Inspections and Interactions, 2) High-Frequency SMPS and power management for low-power electronic systems, and 3) Telecommunication Systems. The section has 15 academics, including professors, postdoctoral fellows, PhD students, and engineers, to support research, industrial collaboration, and educational activities, and is growing steadily.

The SDU campus in Odense contains six faculties and soon a large university hospital, creating a great concentration of academics and students facilitating interdisciplinary research and rich student life. The city of Odense is culturally rich, surrounded by a vibrant and growing robotics community, and highly livable with a green-banked meandering river cutting through the centre and attractive residential areas.

 

Job Description

The position focuses on power management for resource-constrained autonomous, mobile, and embedded electronic systems. Relevant research areas include high-frequency power conversion, battery-operated systems, energy harvesting, power management architectures, embedded control, and analog/digital control of converters. The application domain spans from ultra-low-power electronics and sensors to mobile platforms, robotics, drones, IoT devices, and power management for embedded, compact, and high-performance computing systems.

The role strengthens DHFE’s research profile at the interface between power electronics, microelectronics, embedded systems, and intelligent electronic devices. It is expected to support shared research themes across SDU, including energy-efficient electronics, autonomous systems, battery-powered platforms, sensor networks, health technology, and miniaturized or distributed devices.

The successful candidate should work constructively both with colleagues within DHFE and also with colleagues from other research units, such as SDU Microelectronics, SDU Centre for Industrial Electronics, the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, Faculty of Health (specifically Health Tech), Mechanical Engineering, and other relevant environments, translating power electronics competence into system-level contributions for electronic devices and platforms.

 

Duties

As a faculty member, you will be responsible for developing and delivering undergraduate and graduate teaching in Electronic and Electrical Engineering, with particular attention to strengthening control and power electronics within the BSc portfolio. This includes supervising students at Bachelor and Master’s level, mentoring students, integrating with the student body, and participating in education and outreach activities. Research duties include establishing an externally funded research agenda, publishing in leading journals and conferences, supervising early-career researchers, and contributing to the development of DHFE’s research environment. The candidate is also expected to contribute to external collaboration and perform service at the section, department, university, and professional levels.

 

Qualifications Required

• 
The applicant should hold a doctoral degree (PhD) in Power Electronics, Electronics, or a related subject area. 

• 
Demonstrated potential for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses at the university level. 

• 
The applicant must have relevant research expertise in areas related to efficient and high-frequency power converters, converter control, and power management for computing or embedded electronic systems.

• 
The applicant must have teaching skills that align with the content and responsibilities of the position. This includes possessing both pedagogical and professional skills essential for carrying out the tasks associated with the role. 

• 
A strong track record for research fundraising is required. 

 

For further information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Tim McRae (mcrae@sdu.dk)  or the Head of the Digital and High-frequency Electronics Section, Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, e-mail: esme@sdu.dk.  

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

• 
Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must be in English and include:

• 
A motivation letter that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position (max. 2 pages). 

• 
Detailed Curriculum Vitae, including personal contact information, describing the research, along with any other relevant information, e.g. teaching experience, computational skills, etc.

• 
A research plan with a focus on the development of your research line and research team. 

• 
List of funded projects. 

• 
Teaching Portfolio documenting teaching, learning, and supervision qualifications and approach. Any format is acceptable; see the Faculty's teaching portfolio page for inspiration.

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).

• 
List of publications with the most relevant publications highlighted. 

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Up to three names and emails of researchers can provide an informed reference letter at short notice. (Reference letters and other relevant qualifications may also be included.) 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

  

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period, and the preferred start date is from January 1, 2027. The final start date will be agreed with the successful applicant.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

Lomac A/S is a Danish manufacturing company specializing in steel constructions, working within areas such as marine, offshore, construction, and wind turbines. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Animal Welfare Risks of Feeding Red Seaweed to Dairy Cows
jobs.description:
The Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Aarhus University, calls for applications for a full-time postdoctoral position. The two-year position is available from 1 February 2027, or soon thereafter. The position will be in the research unit Behaviour, stress and welfare (BSW).

Dairy cattle contribute substantially to agricultural greenhouse gas emissions, primarily through enteric methane production, making the identification of effective nutritional mitigation strategies an important area of research. While the feed additive Bovaer has received considerable attention for its methane-reducing effects, concerns regarding animal health and welfare have led to increasing interest in alternative solutions, including seaweed-based feed additives. The seaweed Asparagopsis spp. has shown significant methane-mitigating potential; however, its use has also raised animal welfare concerns. Consequently, there is a need to evaluate the animal welfare effects of seaweed-based feed additives.

Research tasks
• Evaluating the effects of seaweed-based feed additives on the behaviour and welfare of dairy cattle.
• Investigating behavioural indicators of discomfort and pain associated with feed management.
• Validating welfare assessment measures through experimental approaches, including pharmacological interventions.
• Contributing to scientific publications and dissemination of research results.
• Participating in knowledge exchange activities with public authorities and industry stakeholders.
• Contributing to teaching and supervision of students at the bachelor's, master's, and PhD levels.

Qualifications
We are seeking a candidate who has:

• A PhD degree or equivalent in biology, animal science, veterinary science, or a related field, and research experience in animal behaviour and welfare.
• A strong interest in strategies aimed at reducing the climate impact of dairy production through feeding management.
• At least a basic understanding of feeding management.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to communicate scientific research results effectively.
• The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment.
• For non-Scandinavian candidates, a commitment to learning Danish, including reading, writing, and speaking, is expected during the employment period.

Contact
Further information on the position may be obtained from Professor Margit Bak Jensen, phone: +4522365482, email: margitbak.jensen@anivet.au.dk

What we offer
• A well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment and animal experimental facilities
• An informal and multicultural research environment with high professionalism and close collaboration and networking activities
• A workplace characterized by equality and a good work-life balance, and an open discussion across different fields of research.

The candidate will have the opportunity to be trained and gain experience in:

• Teaching and supervision of students at the BSc and MSc level through active involvement in teaching in animal science and in the veterinary science programme.
• Research-based consultancy to authorities, where it is relevant. 

Who we are
Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences is well-known for its skilled and very innovative interdisciplinary research environments with high international impact. We perform world-class research, which contributes with solutions to solve essential societal challenges within the green transition: food production and veterinary medicine – nationally and globally.

The department generates novel research at the highest international level within sustainable food production, environment, climate, health and welfare for animals and humans. The activities form the basis for the research-based public sector consultancy and degree programs covering bachelor’s, master’s and PhD degree programs within animal science and veterinary medicine. We offer a lively, engaged and innovative learning and study environment, which is closely integrated in the research environment.

Our department has unique and advanced animal experimental research facilities and technologies, situated in close connection to the research environment, and a comprehensive national and international research network and good industrial and professional collaboration.

Please refer to Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences (au.dk) for further information about the department: https://anivet.au.dk/en

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is the Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, AU Viborg,
Blichers Allé 20, DK-8830 Tjele, and the area of employment is Aarhus University (AU) with related departments.

Living in Denmark
Please visit the international staff website: https://internationalstaff.au.dk/prearrival/ for information about arriving to and living in Denmark for both the applicants and their potential families.

 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: 211-0367/26-2K Professor within Microbial interactions in plant and environmental systems
jobs.description:
Professor within Microbial interactions in plant and environmental systems
 Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences
 Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen

  
 The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN); Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as full Professor within the area of microbial interactions in plant and environmental systems.

  Research and teaching at PLEN covers topics within Agriculture, Plant Science, Biotechnology, Biosolutions and Environmental Sciences, dealing with a wide range of subjects focusing especially on plants, soil, and microorganisms from molecules through organisms to populations and anthropogenic ecosystems. It is our vision to maintain and develop our position as one of the leading departments for plant science and the related areas based on excellent basic and applied research.

  The department hosts state-of-the art infrastructure and unique field research facilities, with many opportunities for collaborations across the department. The department is organised into four sections, and the appointed professor will be affiliated to the section of Environmental Sciences located at the Frederiksberg campus.

  The section of Environmental Sciences carries out world-leading research across diverse disciplines, including soil microbiology, chemistry, agrohydrology, ecotoxicology, to assess and mitigate human impacts on ecosystems. By combining measurements, experiments, and modelling, the section supports both basic environmental science and applied solutions for sustainable agriculture, climate mitigation, and clean soil and water. The section of Environmental Sciences conducts world-leading research covering environmental biology, chemistry, and ecosystem science. Focusing on agroecosystems and impacts on soil, water, and the atmosphere, the section connects fundamental discoveries to solutions for targeting climate impacts, microbial diversity, and toxicological challenges.

  The professor is expected to teach both at the BSc and MSc levels primarily in the Biotechnology and the Natural resources and Environmental Sciences programmes at the Frederiksberg Campus and to expand these regular teaching commitments to the new MSc in Biosolutions in Kalundborg.

  Duties include the applicant’s own research, development of the field, assessment tasks, grant applications, and research management such as supervision and training of research fellows and other staff. The successful applicant must also teach, supervise, prepare and participate in examinations, and fulfill other tasks requested by the Department.

  Description of qualifications needed

  The professorship is advertised within the area of microbial solutions for climate-friendly and sustainable production systems. Full exploitation of these solutions requires basic understanding of the complex interactions in the environment which shape microbial communities and their functions in soil and at the plant root interface.

  Hence, the appointed professor should have a broad knowledge of microbial ecology including microbial functioning under soil conditions, drivers for microbiome assembly as well as microbe-microbe and plant-microbe interactions of importance for soil and plant health. It is expected that the professor has a recognized international position in the field and contributes to the design and implementation of new methodologies within microbial ecology. The successful candidate is expected to drive research within:

   	
• Model system development for causality and mechanistic understanding of microbial functioning under natural soil conditions 	
• The microbial component of N and P nutrition in agricultural systems 	
• Drivers for root colonization and microbial assembly in agricultural systems 	
• Microbial functions of importance for soil health and functioning 	
• Microbial solutions for climate mitigation and sustainable plant production   The appointed professor is expected to cover teaching in existing courses both at the MSc and BSc levels in subjects related to microbiology, molecular genetics and biotechnology. Likewise, the appointed professor is expected to be a driver for the development of courses to ensure high-quality teaching in a constantly changing educational landscape. Supervision of BSc and MSc projects is expected on a regular basis. International candidates are expected to be able to contribute actively to teaching in Danish within 3-6 years, including supervision and assessment of students. Applicants are required to have university level teaching experience, documented teaching competencies and must be able to explain and reflect upon own teaching practice and portfolio. Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme for assistant professors is required.

  The candidate should fulfil the following criteria:

   	
• PhD or similar in molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, or a related field 	
• Profound experience in the study of plant microbe-related issues in the context of sustainable agriculture 	
• An excellent publication record that includes corresponding-author, senior author and first author publications of relevance to the position and demonstrate an impact on the scientific field of microbial interactions related to soils, plants and the environment 	
• Proven leadership in an academic research environment and ability to guide an independent research group to achieve specific goals 	
• Extensive experience in the development, organization, restructuring, and management of courses at BSc and MSc levels, supported by a comprehensive teaching portfolio that documents pedagogic competences and ongoing skills development. 	
• Extensive experience with supervision of BSc, MSc, and PhD students, as well as postdocs 	
• A teaching portfolio that documents teaching experience and reflections on teaching skills 	
• Documented ability to obtain independent research grants from private and public foundations. 	
• A strong track record of successful external/international collaborations. 	
• Documented experience in organizational tasks such as departmental committees 	
• Experience with outreach activities and communication of research to the public and stakeholders via, e.g., popular science events, press releases, interviews, conferences etc 	
• Societal impact in terms of participation in appropriate stakeholder networks   Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  General criteria apply to the appointment of professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5c_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-professors.pdf
 
 Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  
 Salary and employment conditions

  The position is open from 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is as Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.   There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Further information on the department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department Morten Petersen (morten.petersen@plen.ku.dk).

  
 Filing of application
 The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  Please include

• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines

  The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Only EU citizens will be considered for the position!

About the position
As part of our highly committed multidisciplinary team, you will share responsibility for our daily communication with patients by email, telephone and Teams, as well as for consultations and treatments at the clinic.

At Sellmer Klinik, the path from idea to implementation is short, and we place both our patients and a positive working environment at the heart of everything we do.

We are looking for a fertility specialist to join our team of two doctors who work together to assess and treat patients experiencing infertility. In addition to weekday work, the position includes daytime shifts on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position(s) in Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing for Living System Integration in Architecture
jobs.description:
SDU CREATE invites highly motivated candidates who wish to contribute to a regenerative built environment to apply for one or more PhD positions in Computational Design and Fabrication for Living System Integration in Architecture. The position(s) is expected to begin in January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The application deadline is 15 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

Scope of the work

The PhD position(s) is linked to the Villum CEBE programme, Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment, funded by the Villum Foundation. Within Research Field 2, Design for Regeneration, Circularity and Longevity, the research will develop architectural interfaces that support the establishment and growth of living systems, particularly photosynthetic communities, as a strategy for regenerative architecture. The focus is on enveloping surfaces in the built environment.

The project will focus on designing, testing and demonstrating, at architectural scale, porous mineral interfaces combined with hydrogels. Computational design, fabrication and environmental monitoring will be combined with cultivation experiments and biological assessment, targeting mosses, algae and cyanobacteria in collaboration with partner researchers in biology.

We seek candidates with primary expertise in one of two complementary research profiles:

• 
Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing: exploring how architectural geometry, material composition and 3D printing can create bioreceptive interfaces. The work will combine computational design, printable material development, toolpath generation and robot programming to develop porous mineral interfaces informed by biological requirements.

• 
Living Material Design and Biological Performance: developing hydrogels incorporating living organisms for integration into porous mineral interfaces. The work will combine formulation, cultivation, sensors, automated monitoring and data analysis to evaluate hygrothermal behaviour, biological growth, photosynthetic activity and material performance.

Both profiles require an interest in integrating biological systems and processes into architectural design and construction. The successful candidate(s) will collaborate within the team to develop and validate the resulting interfaces.

The candidate(s) will also contribute to the Centre’s activities, including teaching in the MSc CREATE programme and the BSc programme in Civil and Architectural Engineering through teaching, workshops and co-supervision of student projects.

Focus Area and Research Project

The research will investigate how material composition, porous morphologies and hygrothermal dynamics can support biological establishment and environmental performance, while addressing durability, maintenance and integration into building envelopes. Environmental measurements will help establish relationships between interface design, climatic exposure, biological development and performance.

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to selected areas according to their expertise, working within a team with complementary skills:

• 
Computational design of bioreceptive mineral interfaces for enveloping surfaces in the built environment

• 
Development and characterisation of printable mineral materials

• 
Robotic 3D printing, toolpath generation and fabrication process development

• 
Formulation of hydrogels incorporating living organisms and their integration into printed scaffolds

• 
Cultivation experiments and assessment of biological growth and photosynthetic activity

• 
Sensor integration, automated monitoring and data analysis to evaluate hygrothermal behaviour, ecological and microclimatic performance

• 
Fabrication and evaluation of full-scale architectural demonstrators, addressing durability, maintenance and sustained biological growth

About SDU CREATE’s Research Environment

The Centre for Computational Research in Emergent Architectural Technology and Engineering, SDU CREATE, is led by Associate Professor Roberto Naboni. The Centre investigates advanced concepts and applications in architectural engineering, focusing on computational design, construction robotics, and material innovation. SDU CREATE brings together an international research team working across architectural engineering, computer science, robotics, materials science, and biology. Its research develops sustainable, regenerative approaches to designing and constructing the built environment.

Located within the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark, SDU CREATE provides advanced laboratory facilities for robotic fabrication, additive and subtractive manufacturing, mixed reality applications in design and construction, and structural and mechanical testing. The facilities include industrial robotic systems, computational design platforms, and equipment for the experimental testing of materials, components, and structures. This environment supports interdisciplinary collaboration and partnerships with academic and industrial institutions in Denmark and internationally. The candidate(s) will work within a research culture that combines computational development with physical experimentation and full scale construction.

SDU CREATE is a partner in CEBE, a ten-year national research initiative funded by the Villum Foundation, in which Danish technical universities collaborate to advance the sustainability of the built environment within planetary boundaries. Within this initiative, SDU CREATE leads research in Digitalisation and Automation, RF4, and contributes to research in Design for Regeneration, Circularity, and Longevity, RF2. The programme provides a long-term research framework, access to national research networks, and opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to the development and delivery of CREATE’s research activities and laboratory-based investigations. Responsibilities include:

• 
Conducting high-quality research within the defined research project and contributing original, scientifically rigorous outcomes

• 
Conducting fabrication experiments and biological and environmental performance testing, including operation of robotic systems and laboratory equipment as relevant to the candidate’s research profile

• 
Participating in CREATE’s research team activities, contributing to the development of design, fabrication, and testing frameworks

• 
Developing and maintaining computational tools and workflows supporting the research activities

• 
Assisting in teaching bachelor’s and master’s level courses and workshops, including co-supervision of thesis students and collaboration with interns in research-related activities

• 
Disseminating research results through high-impact peer-reviewed publications and recognised international conferences

• 
Sharing research outcomes through curated and high-quality outputs for digital platforms, exhibitions, and competitions

• 
Contributing to the further development and maintenance of CREATE’s laboratory infrastructures and experimental facilities

• 
Engaging with academic and industrial collaborators at the national and international level, including participation in the Villum CEBE research network

• 
Assisting senior staff in the preparation of applications for external research funding

Engagement in these activities will evolve with the experience of the candidate(s), contributing to the Centre’s excellence and supporting their academic development, ideally towards future career advancement.

Candidate Requirements

Applications are invited from highly motivated candidates holding a Master’s degree in architecture, computational design, civil or architectural engineering, materials science, environmental engineering, biology, or other relevant disciplines related to the research areas. Candidates must demonstrate primary expertise in either Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing or Living Material Design and Biological Performance, and the ability to contribute to shared design, fabrication and validation activities. Interdisciplinary experience connecting these areas is particularly valued.

Candidates must demonstrate:

• 
Documented interest and foundational knowledge in bioreceptive design, living system integration or related research areas

• 
Competence in Grasshopper and Rhino, advanced for the Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing profile and at working level for the Living Material Design and Biological Performance profile, together with relevant programming skills such as Python or C#

• 
For the Bioreceptive Design and Robotic 3D Printing profile: practical experience in computational design, toolpath generation and robotic 3D printing, together with an understanding of biological requirements relevant to design; experience developing porous geometries and printable mineral materials are particularly valued

• 
For the Living Material Design and Biological Performance profile: practical experience in material formulation and biological experimentation or cultivation, together with competence in experimental measurement and data analysis; experience with hydrogels, sensor integration, automated monitoring or hygrothermal characterisation are particularly valued

• 
Hands-on laboratory experience, including physical prototyping or specimen preparation, and experimental testing relevant to the selected profile

• 
Demonstrated capacity to conduct, document and disseminate projects and research outcomes suitable for peer-reviewed publication

• 
Strong proficiency in English, both written and oral

• 
Strong ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams and to coordinate and collaborate daily

• 
Strong communication skills across graphical, written and oral formats

• 
A proven track record of involvement in research or innovation projects; experience in teaching assistance, peer-reviewed publications or engagement with academic or industry stakeholders is evaluated positively

Contact information

For further information about the position(s) and SDU CREATE’s activities, please contact the Head of Centre, Associate Professor Roberto Naboni, at ron@iti.sdu.dk. For additional information on the Centre’s work, visit the website at www.create-sdu.com. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Find full information about how to apply as well as assessment and employment terms on our website!

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position (2 years) in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management
jobs.description:
The Department of Technology and Innovation (ITI) at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), section of Engineering Operations Management, invites applications for a 2-year position as Postdoc in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management.  The position is open from December 1, 2026, and the job location is Odense, Denmark.

 

Job description  

Successful candidates will drive internationally competitive research, collaborate in and across disciplines, work closely with industry and attract competitive external research and innovation funding in collaboration with senior researchers. The candidates will play a key role in providing outstanding education, supervise students, and develop junior research staff. 

 

We offer 

We offer a vigorous international research environment with a balance of male and female researchers, excellent facilities, including the new Robotics and Additive Manufacturing Laboratories at University of Southern Denmark, a long-term strategic initiative created to support research, teaching, and industrial collaboration and experimentation. SDU expects to increase its’ collaboration with industrial companies and associations in the coming years. 

This position will imply collaboration with industrial partners in the Renewable Energy Sector. Examples can be vendors of wind turbines, electrification solutions, electrolyzers, biogas equipment, carbon capture, utilization and storage technologies etc. It can also be major owners / operators of renewable energy plants, as offshore wind turbine park operators, green hydrogen / methanol / ammonia plants etc.

Research will be done to support DK and EU in realizing ambitions for production of green energy at off-take prices competitive with energy from fossil fuels via scaling and industrialization, whether the energy is in the form of green electricity or green fuels for industry and transport. There will be specific emphasis on research into the interplay between business strategy, product design, manufacturing systems design, manufacturing technology choices and scenarios or plans for industrial scaling. In addition to that, the position offers the opportunity to shape our educational and research and innovation programs by contributing to teaching and supervision in areas of Manufacturing technologies of the future and Industrial Management to benefit from new developments in research fields, approaches and content.   

 

We expect 

Candidates must have a relevant PhD.

Commensurate with the seniority of the position applied for, the candidates must ideally have: 

• 
An excellent standing in research and innovation

• 
Documented experience and good track record with education and supervision on undergraduate or graduate level

• 
Extensive experience with industrial collaboration: can be from working in partnerships with or within companies, but also industrial and NGO organizations 

• 
Industry outreach and work experience will be assessed positively 

• 
Research & innovation project management experience will be assessed positively 

• 
International work experience, organizational drive and a team-oriented mindset

• 
Good written and oral communication skills

• 
Fluent in English, both spoken and written                   

Candidates must have experience and competence in several, but not all, of the following fields: 

• 
Business, Manufacturing and Operations Strategy

• 
Product / Service design for Manufacturing, Logistics and Sustainability

• 
Systems Design and Engineering

• 
Materials Science, Industrial processes & Future Manufacturing Technologies

• 
Design, Operations & Maintenance of Manufacturing Systems

• 
Lean Manufacturing / Logistics and Industry 4.0 / 5.0 

• 
Discrete Event Simulation Methods, Agent Based Simulation & Technologies

• 
Machine Learning, AI, LLMs & Data Science for Manufacturing and Supply Chain Operations

• 
Cost-Benefit and Return of Investment Analysis

• 
Life Cycle Analysis Methods 

• 
Modelling and Simulation methods

• 
Case study, Design Science, Action Research Methods

• 
Project Management, Agile Methods, Scrum Methods

• 
EU strategies and plan for decarbonization of industry and society 

• 
UN Sustainability Goals and Dimensions,

Working experience from industry, also within the renewable energy sector, will be seen as positive add-on but is not a requirement to apply for the position. 

 

Contact information
Further information about the position may be obtained from Head of Section, Niels Gorm Maly Rytter, phone: +45 29103729 or email: ngry@iti.sdu.dk 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Curriculum Vitae including information on previous employment, list of programming skills mastered by the applicant, and teaching and supervision experience.

• 
Letter of motivation, including details on qualifications within the subject area (max. one page).

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position on which the applicant wishes to rely on.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
At least one letter of recommendation from supervisors or previous employers. Should your referees wish to send their letters directly to us, please have them use e-mail: tek-hr@tek.sdu.dk mentioning your name and the title of the position in the subject line. Please note that these also need to reach us before deadline.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is October 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from December 1, 2026. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.
